options.C: Only a passive index fund can match the return of the market
options.D: Fundamental analysis of public data can still give abnormal returns

questions.rationale: Weak-form efficiency means prices reflect past price and volume data, so technical analysis fails. It does not rule out abnormal returns from fundamental analysis. Only the semi-strong form rules those out.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 6.9 exam trap (weak vs semi-strong)

questions.stem: Caspian Moreau buys any stock with a low price-to-book ratio and a high dividend yield. He pays no attention to the sector or the economy. Which technique does he use?

options.A: Top-down sector rotation
options.B: Bottom-up growth investing
options.C: Market timing
options.D: Bottom-up value investing

questions.rationale: Company ratios such as low price-to-book and high dividend yield drive his choices, so he is a bottom-up value manager. A sector rotator starts from a forecast of the business cycle and overweights sectors.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 6.10 value investing and exam trap

questions.stem: Ines Kowalczyk cuts her fund's equity weight from 85% to 30% because she expects a recession. She plans to buy equities again at the recovery. Which risk is most specific to her technique?

options.A: She can buy a cheap stock whose business is in permanent decline
options.B: She must be right about both the exit and the return to equities
options.C: Her stocks can lose both earnings and P/E multiple if growth slows
options.D: Her fund's return can differ from the index because of sampling

questions.rationale: This is market timing: a large switch out of equities on a forecast. A timer must be right twice, and out of the market can miss a few very strong days. A value trap is the main risk of value investing.

questions.stem: Radomir Ellison holds only a growth fund. Its stocks trade at high P/E multiples. Economists now forecast slower earnings growth. Why can the fund's price fall sharply?

options.A: The stocks can become value traps with low P/E
options.B: The fund holds too much in defensive sectors
options.C: Both the earnings and the P/E multiple can fall
options.D: The fund's dividends must rise to keep investors

questions.rationale: Growth stock prices already include the expected growth. If growth slows, earnings fall and investors pay a lower P/E multiple, so the price drops from two sources. A value trap is a cheap, low-P/E stock in permanent decline.

questions.stem: Two ETFs track the same index. ETF P has a tracking difference of −0.15% and a tracking error of 0.40%. ETF Q has a tracking difference of −0.35% and a tracking error of 0.08%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Q lags the index less on average, but P follows the index more consistently
options.B: P lags the index less on average, but Q follows the index more consistently
options.C: P lags the index less and also follows the index more consistently
options.D: Q lags the index less and also follows the index more consistently

questions.rationale: Tracking difference is the gap between fund and index returns, so P's smaller gap means it lags less. Tracking error is the variability of that gap, so Q's lower figure means it follows the index more consistently.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 6.11 tracking difference vs tracking error

questions.stem: Tobiah Lindqvist says that his S&P/TSX Composite index fund is safe because it is passive. Which reply is accurate?

options.A: The fund carries full market risk; passive management mainly removes security-selection risk
options.B: The fund carries no market risk; its only risk is tracking error against the index
options.C: The fund moves to cash when the market falls, so it protects the client from declines
options.D: The fund removes systematic risk, because it holds every stock in the index

questions.rationale: Index funds are not risk-free. They carry full market (systematic) risk and give no protection when the market falls. Passive management largely removes manager (security-selection) risk, not market risk. Diversification cannot remove systematic risk.

questions.stem: A manager must fund a fixed payment due in six years. Which step immunizes the bond portfolio against changes in interest rates?

options.A: Set the portfolio's average maturity equal to six years
options.B: Buy one six-year coupon bond and hold it to maturity
options.C: Set the portfolio's duration as short as possible
options.D: Set the portfolio's Macaulay duration equal to six years

questions.rationale: Immunization matches duration, not maturity, to the horizon. A coupon bond's duration is shorter than its maturity, so a six-year coupon bond does not immunize a six-year payment. The manager must also rebalance as duration drifts.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 6.12 immunization and exam trap

questions.stem: A bond manager expects credit spreads to narrow. The manager has no view on the general level of interest rates. Which active technique fits this forecast?

options.A: Move from corporate bonds toward government bonds
options.B: Lengthen the portfolio's duration
options.C: Build a ladder of staggered maturities
options.D: Move from government bonds toward corporate bonds

questions.rationale: This is bond sector rotation. When spreads narrow, corporate bonds gain relative to government bonds, so the manager moves toward corporates. Lengthening duration is a bet on falling rates, and the manager has no rate view.

questions.stem: Rosalind Okafor is 59 and plans to retire in two years. She says she enjoys market swings. Her savings are small compared with her retirement needs. Which risk profile should her RR record?

options.A: A high risk profile, because her stated willingness to accept risk decides the profile
options.B: A medium risk profile, because the RR averages her risk tolerance and her risk capacity
options.C: A low risk profile, because the profile reflects the lower of her risk tolerance and risk capacity
options.D: A high risk profile, because her retirement goal needs a higher return than her savings earn

questions.rationale: The risk profile reflects the lower of risk tolerance and risk capacity. Her small savings give her low capacity, so her profile is low. Her high tolerance does not decide it. The guidance does not average the two parts.
questions.source_quote: "The client’s risk profile should reflect the lower of the client’s assessed risk tolerance and risk capacity." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.3.5, ~L262

questions.stem: Mateus Ferreira wants $500,000 in eight years. His goal needs about 8% a year. His risk profile is medium-low and supports about 4.5%. What should his RR do?

options.A: Raise his risk profile to medium-high so that the portfolio can target the 8% return
options.B: Discuss other ways to close the gap, such as higher savings, a later date or a smaller target
options.C: Put him in an aggressive equity portfolio if he signs a letter that accepts the extra risk
options.D: Keep his profile and use borrowed money in the account to increase the expected return

questions.rationale: The goal must change, not the risk profile. The guidance says a risk profile should not be manipulated to justify higher-risk products. A signed letter does not make a portfolio above his profile suitable.
questions.source_quote: "A client’s risk profile should not be manipulated to justify recommending higher-risk products" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.3.5, L264

questions.stem: Priya Raman holds a portfolio of 40% equity and 60% bonds that matches her risk profile. In a strong stock market year, her return is below the S&P/TSX Composite Index. How should her RR assess the performance?

options.A: Compare the return with a blended benchmark of 40% equity and 60% bonds
options.B: Treat the lower return as proof that the portfolio is unsuitable for her
options.C: Move the portfolio to 100% equity so that it can match the equity index
options.D: Compare the return with the S&P/TSX Composite Index because it is the main market

questions.rationale: Judge performance against a benchmark that matches the agreed asset mix. An equity index is not a fair benchmark for a 40/60 portfolio. A lower return alone does not prove that a portfolio is unsuitable.

questions.stem: Linnea Haugen has a growth objective and a medium risk profile. She asks her RR to exclude all fossil-fuel companies from her portfolio. Which statement about this restriction is correct?

options.A: The restriction lets the RR go above her risk profile if few suitable products remain
options.B: The restriction makes the broad Canadian index the only fair benchmark for her portfolio
options.C: The restriction removes the need for a suitability determination on each later trade
options.D: The restriction narrows her choices, but the portfolio must still fit her risk profile

questions.rationale: Clients can invest in accordance with ESG criteria or other personal preferences. A values-based restriction narrows the choices but never relaxes suitability. An energy exclusion can also make a broad Canadian index an unfair benchmark.
questions.source_quote: "or investing in accordance with environmental, social and governance criteria or other personal preferences." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.3.3, L228

questions.stem: Cedric Fontaine wants an equity fund that holds companies in every sector. In each sector, he wants only the issuers with the best ESG scores. Which ESG approach matches his request?

options.A: An exclusion screen
options.B: A thematic fund
options.C: An impact fund
options.D: A best-in-class approach

questions.rationale: A best-in-class approach keeps every sector but holds the issuers with the best ESG scores. An exclusion screen removes whole industries, so it does not keep every sector.

questions.stem: Odile Mercer bought a stock last year. Its highest price last spring was $42. She says she will sell only at $42 and changes this target very little when news arrives. Which bias does she show?

options.A: Gambler's fallacy
options.B: Confirmation bias
options.C: Anchoring
options.D: Survivorship bias

questions.rationale: Anchoring is a fixation on a reference number, such as a past high, with too little adjustment. Gambler's fallacy is the expectation of a reversal after a run of price changes.

questions.stem: Barnaby Coyle gets a $3,000 tax refund and spends it on a holiday. He calls it "free money". He has a credit card balance at 20% interest. Which bias does this show?

options.A: Mental accounting
options.B: Overconfidence
options.C: Herding
options.D: Hindsight bias

questions.rationale: Mental accounting treats money differently by its source. Barnaby spends the refund and ignores the cost of his card debt. Overconfidence is the over-rating of one's own skill or information.

questions.stem: A client often keeps losing investments to avoid the pain of a realized loss. Which approach usually works best to manage this type of bias?

options.A: Give the client more research reports that show the facts about each holding
options.B: Show the client one holding at a time so that each decision is easier
options.C: Describe each choice to the client only as a chance of gain
options.D: Agree on a written plan with automatic contributions and rebalancing rules

questions.rationale: Loss aversion is an emotional bias, so it is harder to change with information. A written plan, automatic contributions and rebalancing rules usually help. More information helps more with cognitive errors.

questions.stem: An investor studies the past returns of a fund category. His data includes only the funds that still exist today. What is the most likely effect on his expectations?

options.A: He expects returns that are too low, because of home country bias
options.B: He expects returns that are too high, because of survivorship bias
options.C: He expects returns that are too high, because of the gambler's fallacy
options.D: He expects returns that are too low, because of loss aversion

questions.rationale: Survivorship bias judges a category only by surviving funds. Funds that closed are often poor performers, so the investor expects returns that are too high. The gambler's fallacy is an expectation of a reversal after a run.

questions.stem: Two balanced funds fit Henrietta Lund's KYC. The dealer's own fund has a higher fee and pays her RR more. A third-party fund has a lower fee. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The RR can recommend the dealer's fund because both funds are on the product shelf
options.B: The RR can recommend the dealer's fund because the dealer discloses proprietary products
options.C: The RR can recommend the dealer's fund only if it puts Henrietta's interest first
options.D: The RR must recommend the third-party fund because proprietary funds are not allowed

questions.rationale: The RR must put the client's interest first, ahead of a higher level of remuneration. The higher payout cannot decide the choice. Proprietary funds are allowed, but this choice needs a client-centred reason.
questions.source_quote: "must put the client’s interest first, ahead of their own interests and any other competing considerations, such as a higher level of remuneration or other incentives" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.1.3, L460

questions.stem: Kwabena Asare is 61, lives outside Quebec and has just retired. He has made CPP contributions and has lived in Canada all his adult life. Which statement about his government pensions is correct?

options.A: He can start CPP now with a permanent reduction, but OAS cannot start before 65
options.B: He can start CPP and OAS now, and each pension has a reduction for each month before 65
options.C: He can start OAS now with a reduction, but CPP cannot start before 65
options.D: He cannot start CPP or OAS before 65, but each pension increases if he waits

questions.rationale: CPP can start as early as 60, with a reduction of 0.6% for each month before 65. The earliest start for OAS is 65. So he can take CPP now but must wait for OAS.
questions.source_quote: "If you are eligible for the Canada Pension Plan (CPP), you can start your CPP as early as age 60. However, the earliest you can start your OAS pension is age 65." — research/sources/gov/oas-gis-pages.txt canada.ca OAS when-start, L280

questions.stem: Ines Moreau is 67 and has a low income. She receives OAS and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS). Which statement about her GIS is correct?

options.A: GIS is taxable, and a 15% recovery tax applies above the OAS threshold
options.B: GIS is income-tested and is not taxable income
options.C: GIS is a fixed amount that every OAS pensioner receives
options.D: GIS replaces CPP for people who made no CPP contributions

questions.rationale: GIS tops up low-income OAS pensioners and is income-tested. GIS payments are not taxable income. The 15% recovery tax applies to the OAS pension, not to GIS.
questions.source_quote: "Payment amounts for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance and the Allowance for the Survivor are not considered taxable income." — research/sources/gov/oas-gis-pages.txt canada.ca OAS, L564

questions.stem: Yusuf Demir, 38, has a medium risk profile and no emergency fund. He needs $40,000 for a home renovation in 18 months. What should his RR recommend for this money?

options.A: Invest the $40,000 in an equity fund because it has a higher expected return
options.B: Invest the $40,000 in an exempt real estate fund because it pays a higher yield
options.C: Invest the $40,000 in a balanced fund because its risk rating matches his profile
options.D: Hold the $40,000 and an emergency fund in low-volatility assets such as short GICs

questions.rationale: Money needed within a few years belongs in low-volatility assets. An emergency fund is also a common practice. The balanced fund's risk rating alone is not enough, because his short horizon and liquidity need also count.
questions.source_quote: "Investors with a longer investment time horizon may have a greater degree of flexibility when building a portfolio, whereas a short investment time horizon may mean that conservative investments may be the only suitable option." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.3.6, L284

questions.stem: An RR builds a new portfolio for Gwendolyn Shaw. The RR compares her after-tax income with her spending. What is the main benefit of this cash flow analysis?

options.A: It shows the surplus she can invest and whether her goal is realistic
options.B: It sets her risk tolerance from her past investment returns
options.C: It measures her portfolio return against a matching benchmark
options.D: It replaces the need to update her KYC information

questions.rationale: Cash flow analysis compares after-tax income with spending to find the surplus to invest. It shows whether a goal is realistic and how much liquidity the portfolio must supply. It does not measure performance.

questions.stem: Aurelio Vance is retired and has a low risk profile. He wants fixed-income cash each year. He also wants to balance interest-rate risk and reinvestment risk. Which strategy fits best?

options.A: Dollar-cost averaging into an equity fund
options.B: Active sector rotation in a bond fund
options.C: A single long-term bond held to maturity
options.D: A ladder of bonds or GICs with staggered maturities

questions.rationale: A ladder of bonds or GICs with staggered maturities gives regular cash. It balances interest-rate risk and reinvestment risk. A single long-term bond has more interest-rate risk and gives no regular maturities.

questions.stem: Delphine Okoro tells her RR that she lost her job. She will need most of her savings within a year. The dealer has not yet updated her KYC. What should the dealer consider doing now?

options.A: Restrict the account to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements until the KYC review
options.B: Continue to accept all types of trades until her next annual KYC update
options.C: Close her account at once because her KYC information is no longer current
options.D: Sell all her holdings for cash at once without an instruction from her

questions.rationale: A job loss is a significant change. The guidance says the dealer should consider restricting the account to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements until it re-evaluates the KYC. It must update the KYC within a reasonable time.
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer should consider restricting activities in the client’s account to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements, until such time as the Dealer has had a chance to re-evaluate the client’s KYC information." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.11.2, L423

questions.stem: Tobias Wren transfers an account of securities into his dealer. His RR plans to check only the new purchases that Tobias makes later. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The transfer needs no review because the dealer did not recommend the securities
options.B: The transfer is a trigger, so the dealer must review the existing holdings in the account
options.C: The transfer needs a review only if Tobias asks for one in writing
options.D: The transfer is a trigger only if a security in it has a high risk rating

questions.rationale: A deposit or transfer of securities into the account is a trigger event under IDPC 3402(2). The review covers the existing holdings, not only new purchases. No client request is needed.
questions.source_quote: "received or delivered into the client’s account by way of deposit or transfer" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2)(i), L6815-6816

questions.stem: Two funds give Halima Yusuf the same exposure. One fund has a management fee of 0.25%, and the other has 1.50%. How must her RR treat this cost difference?

options.A: Consider only the fees that Halima pays directly, not compensation paid to the dealer
options.B: Ignore the difference because both funds are on the dealer's product shelf
options.C: Consider the potential and actual impact of the costs on her returns and document the basis
options.D: Consider the difference only if Halima asks about fees before the trade

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(1) makes the potential and actual impact of costs a suitability factor. Cost includes indirect fees and compensation to the dealer or RR. The RR must document the reasonable basis for the conclusion.
questions.source_quote: "the potential and actual impact of costs on the retail client’s returns" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(1)(i)(d), L6806

questions.stem: An RR recommends a structured note to Ottilie Brandt, who has limited investment experience. Which approach best meets the guidance for this recommendation?

options.A: Describe the potential returns and leave the risk details to the offering document
options.B: Describe the benefits and ask her to sign a form that she accepts all risks
options.C: Disclose the material positive and negative factors, check that she understands the risks, and document this
options.D: Disclose the risks only if she asks, because the note is on the dealer's shelf

questions.rationale: The guidance asks the RR to disclose any material negative and positive factors. The RR must make sure the client understands the risks and document this. A recommendation that shows only benefits fails this standard.
questions.source_quote: "a Registered Individual should disclose any material negative and positive factors involved in the transaction to the client to assist the client in making an informed decision." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.2.1, L482

questions.stem: Ragnar Holt has a medium-low risk profile. He tells his dealer to keep a stock that is 35% of his account. This decision does not meet the suitability requirement. What must the dealer do?

options.A: Follow the instruction because a decision to hold is not an investment action
options.B: Mark the instruction as unsolicited and then follow it without other steps
options.C: Sell the stock because the dealer cannot follow an unsuitable instruction
options.D: Complete the IDPC 3402(5) steps, including recorded confirmation, before following it

questions.rationale: A decision to hold is an investment action. The dealer may follow an unsuitable instruction only after the 3402(5) steps. Marking the order as unsolicited is not sufficient.
questions.source_quote: "A Registered Individual is not obligated to accept a client order or instruction that does not, in the Registered Individual’s view, meet the criteria for a suitability determination. It is not sufficient for the Registered Individual to mark the order as “unsolicited”." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.10, L718

questions.stem: Siddharth Rao needs $80,000 in 12 years. He can earn 6% a year, compounded annually. He makes equal deposits at the end of each year. What deposit does he need each year?
questions.rationale: Use PMT = FV × r ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1). So 80,000 × 0.06 ÷ (1.06^12 − 1) = $4,742.16. $6,666.67 ignores interest. $4,473.74 assumes deposits at the start of each year.

questions.stem: Marguerite Doyle invests $250,000 at 5% a year, compounded annually. She wants equal payments at the end of each year for 25 years. The balance is zero after the last payment. What is each payment?
questions.rationale: Use PMT = PV × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n). So 250,000 × 0.05 ÷ (1 − 1.05^−25) = $17,738.11. $16,893.44 assumes payments at the start of each year. $10,000.00 ignores interest.

questions.stem: Bartholomew Achebe is 70 and receives OAS. His net income is close to the OAS recovery threshold. He has $20,000 to invest for extra income. Which account helps him most to protect his OAS?

options.A: A TFSA, because its income does not affect federal income-tested benefits
options.B: An RRSP, because its withdrawals are not included in net income
options.C: An FHSA, because its withdrawals are always tax-free
options.D: A non-registered account, because dividends are grossed down for the OAS test

questions.rationale: TFSA income does not affect federal income-tested benefits and credits. So it does not increase the OAS recovery tax. RRSP withdrawals are taxable income, and he must also convert an RRSP by the end of the year he turns 71.
questions.source_quote: "Any income that you earn in your TFSA will not impact your federal income-tested benefits and credits." — research/sources/cra/tfsa-pages.txt CRA TFSA benefits, L209

questions.stem: Celestine Moreau gives growth shares to her 12-year-old son. In later years, the shares pay dividends and she sells none of them. Then her son sells them at a gain. How are these amounts taxed?

options.A: The dividends and the capital gain are both taxed to Celestine
options.B: The dividends and the capital gain are both taxed to her son
options.C: The dividends are taxed to her son, and the capital gain is taxed to Celestine
options.D: The dividends are taxed to Celestine, and the capital gain is taxed to her son

questions.rationale: Income on property given to a related minor under 18 is attributed back to the transferor. A minor's capital gains are not attributed. So the dividends are Celestine's income, and the gain is her son's.
questions.source_quote: "to or for the benefit of a person who was under 18 years of age" — research/sources/gov/ita-attribution-income-splitting.txt ITA s.74.1(2), L10

questions.stem: Florian Kask sells shares at a $6,000 loss to offset a gain. Two weeks later, his spouse buys the same shares and still holds them 30 days after his sale. What happens to the loss?

options.A: Florian can claim the loss because his spouse is a separate taxpayer
options.B: Florian cannot claim the loss because his spouse is an affiliated person
options.C: Florian can claim the loss because his spouse bought after 14 days
options.D: Florian cannot claim the loss, and the loss is lost permanently for everyone

questions.rationale: A spouse is an affiliated person. The superficial loss rule denies the loss if an affiliated person buys identical property within 30 days. The rule also needs that person to still own it 30 days after the sale.
questions.source_quote: "You, or a person affiliated with you, buys, or has a right to buy, the same or identical property (called "substituted property") during the period starting 30 calendar days before the sale and ending 30 calendar days after the sale" — research/sources/cra/capital-gains-losses-superficial-loss-pages.txt CRA capital gains pages, L727

questions.stem: A Canadian-controlled private corporation sells an investment at a capital gain. Which notional account tracks the non-taxable part of the gain that it can pay out as a tax-free capital dividend?

options.A: The general rate income pool (GRIP)
options.B: The eligible refundable dividend tax on hand (ERDTOH)
options.C: The capital dividend account (CDA)
options.D: The non-eligible refundable dividend tax on hand (NERDTOH)

questions.rationale: The CDA tracks mainly the non-taxable part of capital gains. The corporation pays it out by election as tax-free capital dividends. GRIP tracks income taxed at the general rate, which it pays as eligible dividends.
questions.source_quote: "exceeds the total of (B) the portion of the capital gain referred to in clause (A) that is the corporation’s taxable capital gain" — research/sources/gov/ita-corporate-integration-rdtoh-grip-cda.txt ITA s.89(1) CDA, L197-199

questions.stem: In 2025, Leopold Haas buys 300 shares at $15 with a $30 commission. Later he buys 200 shares at $18 with a $30 commission. He sells 250 shares at $20 with a $40 commission. What is his taxable capital gain?
questions.rationale: Average ACB = 8,160 ÷ 500 = $16.32. Gain = 5,000 − 4,080 − 40 = $880. At the 2025 inclusion rate of 1/2, the taxable capital gain is $440. $880 is the full gain, not the taxable part.
questions.qa_note: calc: ACB=(4500+30+3600+30)/500=16.32; 250×16.32=4080; gain=5000−4080−40=880; ×1/2=440. Distractors: 460 omits sale commission; 592.50 uses first-bought cost (FIFO); 880 full gain

questions.stem: In 2025, Agnieszka Wolff realizes a $6,000 capital gain on shares and a $9,000 capital loss on fund units. Her salary is $85,000. Which statement about her 2025 result is correct?

options.A: She can deduct the remaining $1,500 allowable capital loss from her salary in 2025
options.B: She can carry the remaining $1,500 back three years against any type of income
options.C: Her remaining $1,500 is a net capital loss for use against taxable capital gains
options.D: Her remaining $1,500 expires if she has no capital gains within seven years

questions.rationale: The allowable loss of $4,500 reduces the $3,000 taxable gain to zero. The remaining $1,500 is part of her net capital loss. She can use it against taxable capital gains in the three previous years or any future year.
questions.source_quote: "You can use a net capital loss to reduce your taxable capital gain in any of the three previous years or in any future year." — research/sources/cra/capital-gains-losses-superficial-loss-pages.txt CRA, L582

questions.stem: Corinne Dube has 2026 taxable income of $90,000. Use the 2026 federal rates: 14% up to $58,523 and 20.5% from $58,523.01 to $117,045. What is her federal tax before credits?
questions.rationale: Each rate applies only to the income in its bracket. 58,523 × 14% = 8,193.22, and 31,477 × 20.5% = 6,452.79. The total is $14,646.01. $18,450.00 wrongly applies 20.5% to all income.

questions.stem: Emeric Laval is in the 26% federal bracket in 2026. He receives a $2,000 eligible dividend. The gross-up is 38%, and the federal dividend tax credit is 6/11 of the gross-up. What is his federal tax on the dividend?
questions.rationale: Grossed-up amount = 2,000 × 1.38 = 2,760. Tax = 2,760 × 26% = 717.60. The credit is 6/11 × 760 = 414.55, so the tax is $303.05. $520.00 treats the dividend like interest.

questions.stem: A client sends her dealer an email. It alleges that her RR misrepresented the risk of an investment. How soon must the dealer send her an acknowledgement letter?

options.A: Within two business days of receipt
options.B: Within five business days of receipt
options.C: Within 30 days of receipt
options.D: Within 90 days of receipt

questions.rationale: The dealer must send an acknowledgement letter within five business days of receipt of a complaint. Two business days is the time for an Approved Person to report a complaint to the dealer.
questions.source_quote: "The Dealer Member must send an acknowledgement letter to the complainant within five business days of receipt of a complaint." — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3725(1), L7943-7944

questions.stem: Desmond Achterberg, an RR, gets a written complaint about an unsuitable trade. He offers to refund his commission. In return, the client must sign a release that stops her from complaining to CIRO. Which statement is correct?

options.A: He can settle on his own if he pays the refund from his own money
options.B: He can settle if the dealer later approves the release as written
options.C: He needs the dealer's prior written consent, and the release cannot stop a complaint to CIRO
options.D: He can settle if the client agrees, because the release is a private contract

questions.rationale: An Approved Person needs the dealer's written consent before any settlement, whatever its form. A release must not stop a client from complaining to securities regulators or SROs. So the dealer cannot approve this term.
questions.source_quote: "An Approved Person must obtain the Dealer Member's written consent before entering into any settlement agreement with a client, regardless of the form of the settlement and regardless of whether the settlement is the result of a client complaint" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3710(1), L7822-7825

questions.stem: A dealer outside Quebec receives a client complaint. On day 85, it knows that it cannot give a final response within 90 days. What must the dealer do?

options.A: Tell the client the reasons and a new estimated date, and tell CIRO the reasons
options.B: Tell the client to wait, because the 90 days stop while the investigation continues
options.C: Tell CIRO only, because the client has no right to know the reasons for the delay
options.D: Close the file and ask the client to send the complaint to OBSI

questions.rationale: The dealer must tell the client the reasons for the delay and the new estimated time of completion. It must also tell CIRO the reasons. The client can also go to OBSI after 90 days with no final response.
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer Member must inform the client if the Dealer Member is unable to provide the client with a final response within the 90 days time line and must include the reasons for the delay and the new estimated time of completion" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3726(4)(ii), L7998-8000

questions.stem: Oskar Lindqvist is a trader at a Participant. A pension fund client tells him that it will sell 400,000 shares of a thinly traded company. Before Oskar enters the client order, he buys put options on that company for his own account. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Oskar front ran the client order, because a put is a related derivative.
options.B: Oskar did not break UMIR, because front running covers only the same security.
options.C: Oskar made a wash trade, because there was no change in beneficial ownership.
options.D: Oskar did not break UMIR, because he traded for himself and not for the firm.

questions.rationale: Oskar knew of an unentered client order that could affect the price. UMIR 4.1(1) then bars trades in the security or a related derivative. UMIR 10.4 applies this rule to employees. A put is a related derivative, so B is wrong. No exception applies.
questions.source_quote: "market, for the purchase or sale of the security, derivative or any related security or related derivative;" — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR 4.1(1)(a), ~lines 5717-5720

questions.stem: Henrike Absalon is an RR. On the trading floor, she hears an unconfirmed rumour that a mining company will receive a takeover bid. She knows of no client order in the stock. She buys the shares for her own account. Under UMIR 4.1, is this front running?

options.A: Yes, because she traded before the takeover bid became public.
options.B: Yes, because any employee trade based on market information is front running.
options.C: No, because she had no knowledge of a specific unentered client order.
options.D: No, because front running applies only to options, not to shares.

questions.rationale: Front running needs knowledge of a specific client order that is not yet entered. UMIR Policy 4.1 says that trading on non-specific market information, including rumours, is not front running. A is wrong because the timing of a public bid is not the UMIR 4.1 test.
questions.source_quote: "Trading based on non-specific pieces of market information, including rumours, does not constitute frontrunning." — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR Policy 4.1 Part 2, ~line 5781

questions.stem: Rupert Eskildsen asks his RR to enter a large buy order one minute before the market closes on the last day of the quarter. The order price is well above the last sale price. Rupert wants his quarter-end account value to look higher. Which UMIR concern does this order raise most directly?

options.A: Front running of a client order that is not yet entered
options.B: Trading ahead of a client's expression of interest
options.C: Trading to fix a failed trade before the report is due
options.D: Artificial pricing by setting a high closing price

questions.rationale: UMIR 2.2(2) prohibits orders that could reasonably be expected to create an artificial price. Policy 2.2 lists setting the close as an example. The time of entry and the motive point to an artificial price. A is wrong because there is no other client order to trade ahead of.
questions.source_quote: "effect a high or low closing sale price, ask price or bid price" — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR Policy 2.2 Part 2(e)(ii), ~line 4181

questions.stem: Leontyne Abara is an RR. Two accounts of one client often trade the same thinly traded stock with each other. Leontyne believes that the activity may violate UMIR 2.2. What must she do?

options.A: Report the activity to CIRO by the 15th day of the next month
options.B: Watch the accounts for another month to confirm a pattern
options.C: Report the activity forthwith to her supervisor or the compliance department
options.D: Tell the client to stop the trades and record the warning in the file

questions.rationale: Under UMIR 10.16(1), an employee who believes activity may violate a listed rule, such as UMIR 2.2, reports forthwith to a supervisor or compliance. The firm, not the RR, reports findings to CIRO under UMIR 10.16(4). So A is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "shall forthwith report to their supervisor or the compliance department of the Participant upon becoming aware of activity in a principal account, non-client account or client account" — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR 10.16(1), ~line 14073

questions.stem: Gideon Mbatha is an RR. A client with a modest stated income makes many cash deposits of about $3,000 each. The client then wires the money abroad. Gideon has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering, but he cannot prove it. Which statement is correct?

options.A: No report is necessary, because each deposit is below $10,000.
options.B: Gideon must verify the facts before anyone reports to FINTRAC.
options.C: Gideon should ask the client to explain before he escalates the matter.
options.D: The dealer must report the transactions to FINTRAC as soon as practicable.

questions.rationale: PCMLTFA s. 7 requires a report when there are reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering. There is no dollar minimum, and the reporter does not have to verify the facts. Gideon escalates to AML compliance and does not tell the client. So C is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "report to the Centre every financial transaction that occurs or that is attempted in the course of their activities and in respect of which there are reasonable grounds to suspect that" — research/sources/gov/pcmltfa-extracts.txt PCMLTFA s.7, ~lines 77-82

questions.stem: Corentin Abiodun's close friend is the CFO of a listed company. The friend tells Corentin that the company will soon announce a takeover. The news is not public. Corentin asks his RR to buy call options on the company. What should the RR do?

options.A: Decline and report it, because Corentin is a tippee with a material fact
options.B: Accept it, because call options are not securities of the issuer
options.C: Accept it, because only insiders of the issuer are in a special relationship
options.D: Accept it, but put the insider marker 'IA' on the order

questions.rationale: Corentin learned an undisclosed material fact from an officer, so he is a tippee in a special relationship (OSA s. 76(5)). OSA s. 76(6) treats calls as securities of the issuer. UMIR 2.3 bars an order that breaks securities law. A marker does not make the order legal, so D is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "a put, call, option or other right or obligation to purchase or sell securities of the issuer" — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt OSA s.76(6)(a), ~line 437

questions.stem: Ilse Brandvold wants to buy 3,000 shares at $25.00 or less. She accepts any part of the order that fills at once. She wants the unfilled part cancelled immediately. Which order type best meets her needs?

options.A: Fill-or-kill order
options.B: Immediate-or-cancel order
options.C: Iceberg order
options.D: Market order

questions.rationale: An immediate-or-cancel order fills what it can at once and cancels the rest. A fill-or-kill order fills the whole quantity at once or nothing, so it does not accept a partial fill. A market order gives no price control.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 8.3 order table (IOC vs FOK; market terms, not UMIR definitions)

questions.stem: An institutional client wants to buy 300,000 shares of a mid-cap stock during the day. She worries that a large visible order will push the price up. Which order type best addresses her concern?

options.A: A fill-or-kill order for the full quantity
options.B: A market order for the full quantity
options.C: An iceberg order that displays only part of the size
options.D: An immediate-or-cancel order for the full quantity

questions.rationale: An iceberg order displays part of the size, and a hidden reserve refills it. This limits market impact. A market order shows the full demand at once and can fill far from the last price.
questions.source_quote: "disclosed or partially disclosed (i.e., iceberg orders)" — research/sources/ciro/gn-urpart7-26-0007-manipulative-deceptive-trading-practices.txt GN-URPART7-26-0007 Q2.1 'Abusive Liquidity Detection', ~line 94

questions.stem: Wilhelmina Asante holds a volatile small-cap stock that trades at $6.00. She asks for a stop-loss order with a trigger price of $5.40 and no limit price. Which risk should her RR explain?

options.A: The order cancels automatically when the price reaches $5.40.
options.B: The order fills at exactly $5.40, even in a fast market.
options.C: The order becomes a limit order at $5.40 and may never fill.
options.D: The order becomes a market order and may fill well below $5.40.

questions.rationale: A triggered stop-loss order with no limit becomes a market order (GN-URPART7-25-0003). In a fast or thin market, it can fill far from the trigger price. C describes a stop-limit order, which controls the price but may not fill.
questions.source_quote: "entering a stop loss order on a marketplace that, when triggered, will become a "market order"." — research/sources/ciro/gn-urpart7-25-0003-management-of-stop-loss-orders.txt GN-URPART7-25-0003 Q1, ~line 85

questions.stem: Benedikt Osei buys TSX-listed shares in his cash account on a Thursday. The next day, Friday, is a business day. When is the regular settlement date for this trade?

options.A: Thursday, the trade date
options.B: Friday, the next business day
options.C: The following Monday
options.D: The following Tuesday

questions.rationale: Since May 27, 2024, most equity trades settle T+1, the next business day after the trade date (NI 24-101). Monday would be T+2, the former cycle. Tuesday would be T+3.
questions.source_quote: ""T+1" means the next business day following T;" — research/sources/csa/ni-24-101-institutional-trade-matching-and-settlement.txt NI 24-101 s.1.1, ~line 82

questions.stem: Felicity Achterberg sold short 1,000 shares in her margin account. Which change would most likely cause a margin call in her account?

options.A: A fall in the share price
options.B: No change in the share price
options.C: A move of the stock onto the LSERM
options.D: A rise in the share price

questions.rationale: A short position loses value when the price rises. The required credit is (100% + rate) × market value, so a rise increases it and can cause a margin call. A fall in price helps a short seller. Falling prices cause margin calls on long positions.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 8.5 long/short margin table (margin call if the price rises for short)

questions.stem: Ruben Kowalczyk tells his RR to buy 500 shares of a named bank stock today. He lets the RR choose when to enter the order and at what price. Ruben does not have a discretionary account. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The RR may choose the time and price, because Ruben named the security and amount.
options.B: The RR needs a signed discretionary account agreement before entering the order.
options.C: The RR may choose the time and price only after a Supervisor approves each order.
options.D: The RR may also choose a different bank stock, if it gives better execution.

questions.rationale: IDPC 3221(2) exempts time-and-price discretion used for best execution on a client order for a specific amount or a specific security. So Ruben needs no discretionary account. D is wrong because a choice of security is account discretion, which needs a discretionary account.
questions.source_quote: "relating to a client order for a specific amount or a specific security." — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3221(2), ~lines 6065-6066

questions.stem: A dealer sends a client a trade confirmation for a purchase of common shares. Which item must the confirmation show?

options.A: The client's risk tolerance from the KYC form
options.B: The RR's share of the commission
options.C: Whether the dealer acted as principal or agent
options.D: The client's total account value after the trade

questions.rationale: IDPC 3816(2) sets the minimum contents of a confirmation. They include whether the dealer acted as principal or agent, the settlement date, the quantity and the consideration. The account statement, not the confirmation, shows the total market value of positions.
questions.source_quote: "whether or not the person or company that executed the trade acted as principal or agent" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3816(2)(i)(c), ~line 9244

questions.stem: Which statement about an Investment Dealer's best execution obligation is correct?

options.A: The dealer must get the best available price on every single client trade.
options.B: The dealer must have best execution policies and review them at least once a year.
options.C: The dealer has no best execution obligation for order-execution-only accounts.
options.D: The dealer must follow all client instructions, even if they break CIRO requirements.

questions.rationale: Best execution is a policies-and-procedures duty. The dealer's policies must address best execution, and the dealer reviews them at least annually (IDPC 3120, 3126). A is wrong because a dealer may not achieve best execution on every single trade. The duty also applies to OEO accounts.
questions.source_quote: "A Dealer Member must review its best execution policies and procedures at least annually" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3126(1), ~line 5269

questions.stem: Desmond Okonkwo wants to buy exactly 4,000 shares of a stock now. He does not want a partial fill. If the full 4,000 shares cannot fill at once, he wants no shares at all. Which order type best meets his needs?

options.A: An iceberg order
options.B: An immediate-or-cancel order
options.C: A stop-limit order
options.D: A fill-or-kill order

questions.rationale: A fill-or-kill order fills the whole quantity at once, or nothing. This is all-or-nothing, as Desmond wants. B is wrong because an immediate-or-cancel order fills what it can at once and cancels the rest, so it can leave a partial fill.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 8.3 order table (FOK: fills the whole quantity at once, or nothing; IOC: fills what it can at once and cancels the rest)

questions.stem: Imogen Thackeray is an RR. A client wants her to trade his account on a discretionary basis. Which condition must Imogen meet before she can trade a discretionary account?

options.A: She must have at least one year of active experience in any one product type.
options.B: She must get the client's verbal approval before she enters each trade.
options.C: She must have at least two years of active experience in all product types traded.
options.D: She must hold the discretionary account at a dealer other than her own dealer.

questions.rationale: IDPC 3275 requires the RR to have at least two years of active experience in trading, advising or analysis for all product types traded. The account must also be at the RR's own dealer, so D is wrong. B describes a non-discretionary account, not a discretionary condition.
questions.source_quote: "has at least two years of active experience in trading, advising or performing analysis with respect to all types of products that are to be traded on a discretionary basis" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3275(1)(i), ~lines 6594-6595

questions.stem: Ingrid Halvorsen, 54, tells her Registered Representative (RR) that she received a large inheritance. She now plans to retire next year. What must the dealer do?

options.A: Update her KYC information within a reasonable time after it learns of the change
options.B: Wait for her next scheduled 36-month KYC review to record the change
options.C: Update her KYC information only if she signs a new account application
options.D: Take no action because her current holdings were suitable when bought

questions.rationale: An inheritance and a new retirement date are significant changes. IDPC 3209(3) requires a KYC update within a reasonable time after the dealer learns of them. The 36-month cycle in IDPC 3209(4) is a minimum and does not delay this update.
questions.source_quote: "updating the information within a reasonable time after the Dealer Member becomes aware of a significant change in the client’s information required under section 3202" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3209(3), ~L5650

questions.stem: Equity markets fall 15% in a broad correction. Oswin Marchetti's personal situation is the same. His diversified blue-chip holdings have no company-specific news. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The market fall is a trigger event that requires a new KYC update for Oswin
options.B: The dealer must reassess every approved security because of the market fall
options.C: The market fall alone is not a trigger event, so a portfolio-level review comes first
options.D: The dealer needs to do nothing because the holdings were suitable when bought

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(2) does not list a general market change as a trigger event. CIRO guidance generally does not require reassessment of individual securities for it. Good practice is a portfolio-level review. Doing nothing ignores the monitoring loop.
questions.source_quote: "While a change in the overall market or economic conditions may affect a Dealer’s or an Approved Person’s assessment of a security, we generally would not consider it a change requiring reassessment of individual securities." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3300-21-001-product-due-diligence-kyp.txt GN-3300-21-001 'Monitor and review significant changes', ~L185

questions.stem: Dariusz Okafor holds a retail account with an Investment Dealer. Which event requires the dealer to review his account for suitability under IDPC 3402(2)?

options.A: The central bank raises its policy interest rate by half a point
options.B: Dariusz transfers a block of shares into the account from another dealer
options.C: The dealer sends Dariusz his regular quarterly account statement
options.D: Dariusz asks for a copy of his annual fee/charge report

questions.rationale: A deposit or transfer of securities into the account is a trigger event under IDPC 3402(2)(i). The dealer must then review the account against IDPC 3402(1). A general interest rate change is not a listed trigger event.
questions.source_quote: "are received or delivered into the client’s account by way of deposit or transfer" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2)(i), ~L6814

questions.stem: Marisol Lindqvist's account holds only one mutual fund. The fund reports a 1-year return of 8%. Her annual performance report shows 4% for the same year. She invested most of her money just before a market fall. What explains the difference?

options.A: Her report is wrong, because it must use the same time-weighted method as the fund
options.B: The fund figure includes sales charges, but her report shows returns before charges
options.C: Her report leaves out income, but the fund figure includes reinvested distributions
options.D: Her report uses a money-weighted return net of charges, which reflects her cash flows

questions.rationale: IDPC 3810(2) requires a money-weighted return net of charges. It reflects the timing and size of her deposits. The fund figure is a time-weighted unit-value return before sales charges. So the two figures can differ, and neither is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "the amount of the annualized total percentage return calculated net of charges using a money weighted rate of return calculation methodology generally accepted in the securities industry for the following periods:" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3810(2)(v), ~L8773

questions.stem: Tobias Nakamura opened an account seven months ago. The account holds positions with market values that the dealer can determine. Which statement about his annual performance report is correct?

options.A: The dealer does not have to send it yet, because the account is not 12 months old
options.B: The dealer must send it now, because the account holds positions with known values
options.C: The dealer must send it only if Tobias asks for one in writing
options.D: The dealer must send it within three months of the account opening date

questions.rationale: IDPC 3810(1) requires the report only for a client whose account was opened at least 12 months ago. Positions with known values are a separate condition, and all conditions must apply. The dealer may send the first report within 24 months.
questions.source_quote: "the client’s account was opened at least 12 months ago" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3810(1)(iv), ~L8717

questions.stem: A balanced fund has a mandate of 60% Canadian equities and 40% Canadian bonds. Which benchmark is the most appropriate to judge its performance?

options.A: A Canadian equity index, because equities cause most of the fund's return
options.B: Whichever index the fund did better than at the end of the year
options.C: A 60/40 blend of a Canadian equity index and a Canadian bond index, set in advance
options.D: The 91-day Treasury bill rate, because it is the risk-free rate of return

questions.rationale: A benchmark must match the mandate and be chosen in advance. A 60/40 blend of equity and bond indices does this. An equity index alone gives a misleading comparison. A benchmark chosen after the results makes them look better than they are.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 9.2 'The proper use of benchmarks'

questions.stem: Henrietta Osei holds an equity fund with a large unrealized gain in a non-registered account. Her RR suggests a switch to a similar fund with a lower expense ratio. The switch has a fee. What must the RR consider?

options.A: Only the lower expense ratio, because it saves Henrietta money every year
options.B: The switch fee and the tax on the realized gain, compared with keeping the fund
options.C: Only the switch fee, because the tax effect is Henrietta's own personal matter
options.D: Only the past 1-year returns of the two funds, because returns include costs

questions.rationale: Suitability includes the impact of costs on returns (IDPC 3402(1)(i)(d)) and a reasonable range of alternatives, such as keeping the fund. The sale also realizes a taxable capital gain. The lower expense ratio alone ignores the fee and the tax.
questions.source_quote: "the potential and actual impact of costs on the retail client’s returns" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(1)(i)(d), ~L6806

questions.stem: Leopold Vance buys a stock at $25.00. He receives a dividend of $0.75 during the year. At year end the stock trades at $27.25. What is his holding-period return?
questions.rationale: HPR = (27.25 − 25.00 + 0.75) ÷ 25.00 = 12.0%. The 9.0% result leaves out the dividend. The 11.0% result divides by the ending price instead of the starting price.

questions.stem: A portfolio returns +15% in year 1, −8% in year 2 and +6% in year 3. What is its annualized return over the three years?
questions.rationale: Link the returns: 1.15 × 0.92 × 1.06 − 1 = 12.15% cumulative. Annualize: 1.12148^(1/3) − 1 = 3.90%. The 4.33% figure is the arithmetic average. The 4.05% figure divides the cumulative return by three and ignores compounding.

questions.stem: A fund returns 2%, 8% and 14% over three years. What is the sample standard deviation of these returns, with division by n − 1?
questions.rationale: The mean is 8%. The squared deviations are 36 + 0 + 36 = 72. Divide by n − 1: 72 ÷ 2 = 36, and √36 = 6.00%. The 4.90% figure uses the population form, √(72 ÷ 3). The 36.00% figure is the variance.
questions.qa_note: calc: mean 8; sum sq dev 72; sqrt(72/2) = 6.00; population sqrt(72/3) = 4.899; variance 36

questions.stem: Wilhelmina Strand will put all her savings into one fund. The risk-free rate is 2.5%. Fund P returned 11%, with σ 18% and β 0.9. Fund Q returned 9.5%, with σ 12% and β 1.3. Which fund is the better risk-adjusted choice for her?

options.A: Fund P, because its Treynor ratio is about 9.44 against 5.38 for Fund Q
options.B: Fund Q, because its Sharpe ratio is about 0.58 against 0.47 for Fund P
options.C: Fund P, because its return is 1.5 percentage points higher than Fund Q
options.D: Fund Q, because its higher beta gives it more return for each unit of risk

questions.rationale: The fund will be her whole portfolio, so she bears total risk. Use Sharpe: P = 8.5 ÷ 18 = 0.47; Q = 7 ÷ 12 = 0.58. Treynor counts only systematic risk, so it ignores company-specific risk that she bears.
questions.qa_note: calc: Sharpe P 8.5/18 = 0.472, Q 7/12 = 0.583; Treynor P 8.5/0.9 = 9.44, Q 7/1.3 = 5.38. concept: guide 9.3 Sharpe for a client's only fund

questions.stem: A portfolio returned 12% with a beta of 1.4. The risk-free rate was 3% and the market returned 9%. What is the portfolio's Jensen's alpha?
questions.rationale: Required return = 3 + 1.4 × (9 − 3) = 11.4%. Alpha = 12 − 11.4 = +0.6%. The +3.0% figure compares the portfolio with the market and ignores beta. The −0.6% figure multiplies beta by the market return without the risk-free rate.

questions.stem: Lucan Ferreira, an RR, wants his business card to say "Vice-President, Wealth". His dealer has not appointed him to that corporate office. Which statement is correct?

options.A: He must not use the title, because he does not hold that corporate office
options.B: He can use the title if the card also says that the title is honorary
options.C: He can use the title if his clients do not rely on it to choose him
options.D: He can use the title, because CIRO rules do not cover business cards

questions.rationale: IDPC 3640(2)(ii) prohibits a corporate officer title unless the dealer appointed the Approved Person to that office. A note that the title is honorary does not cure this. The rule applies to how he presents himself in any form.
questions.source_quote: "a corporate officer title, unless their Dealer Member has appointed that Approved Person to that corporate office pursuant to applicable corporate law" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3640(2)(ii), ~L7578

questions.stem: Which item must a designated Supervisor approve before the dealer uses it?

options.A: An e-mail to one client that confirms the time of a meeting
options.B: The text of an educational seminar about how bonds work
options.C: A new script that RRs will read when they telephone prospects
options.D: A previously approved template advertisement with a new branch address

questions.rationale: IDPC 3602(3) lists telemarketing scripts for pre-approval. Educational seminar texts are excluded. A minor change to an approved template, such as the branch location, needs no approval. Single-client correspondence gets one of the IDPC 3602(4) review methods.
questions.source_quote: "A Dealer Member must ensure that the following items are approved by a designated Supervisor before use or publication:" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3602(3), ~L7295

questions.stem: Casimir Duval, an RR, discusses a client's rebalancing plan on a messaging app on his personal phone. His dealer has not approved the app. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The messages are outside the retention rules, because the phone is his own
options.B: The messages are business records that the dealer must keep, because content decides this
options.C: The messages need retention only if they contain an actual order to buy or sell
options.D: The messages are acceptable without retention, because the client started the chat

questions.rationale: CIRO guidance says the content of a message decides whether retention applies, not the device. A message about a client's account is a business record. An uncaptured chat on a non-approved channel is also a supervision gap.
questions.source_quote: "depends on the content of the communication. The type of device used to transmit the communication or whether it is a personal device or Dealer issued device is irrelevant." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3600-21-002-advertisements-sales-literature-correspondence-social-media.txt GN-3600-21-002 'Record retention', ~L277

questions.stem: Annika Bergstrom tells her RR to buy a speculative stock. The RR decides that the trade does not meet the suitability criteria. What must the dealer do before it carries out her instruction?

options.A: Get a branch manager's approval, and then mark the order as unsolicited
options.B: Refuse the order, because a dealer can never carry out an unsuitable trade
options.C: Carry out the order at once, because the client has the final decision
options.D: Tell her why and advise against it, recommend a suitable alternative, and record her confirmation

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(5) lets the dealer act on an unsuitable instruction only after three steps. It must explain and advise against the action, recommend a suitable alternative, and receive recorded confirmation. Refusal is not mandatory, but the steps are.
questions.source_quote: "received recorded confirmation of the retail client’s instruction to proceed with the action" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(5)(iii), ~L6852

questions.stem: A dealer's grid pays RRs a higher payout on fee-based revenue and on related-party funds. Which statement about its records is correct?

options.A: Its records must document these arrangements and show how it complies with conflicts requirements
options.B: Disclosure of the grid to clients is sufficient, so the dealer needs no other records
options.C: Compensation records are internal staff matters, so CIRO record rules do not apply
options.D: Its records must cover only incentives that give a direct benefit to the client

questions.rationale: IDPC 3804(2)(xvii) requires records of compensation arrangements and incentive practices. IDPC 3804(2)(xvi) requires records that show compliance with conflicts requirements. Disclosure alone never satisfies the conflicts rule (IDPC 3113(3)).
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer Member’s sales practices, compensation arrangements and incentive practices" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3804(2)(xvii)(a), ~L8367
